title: Israeli Strikes Kill 3 in Gaza Including 4-Year-Old as Netanyahu Threatens to Intensify Attacks Over Kite Launches
detail: On Sunday, August 23, 2026, Israeli aircraft fired missiles at a warehouse in Az-Zawayda, central Gaza, reducing it to rubble and killing 4-year-old Muhammad Abdel Salam Taha and one other person, with six to seven others wounded, according to Gaza's Hamas-run civil defense service; Al Jazeera's correspondent reporting from the scene said the strike caused a fire and widespread destruction. A separate Israeli strike near Salah al-Din Street in Nuseirat killed one more person, and further strikes wounded people in Khan Younis, Al-Shujaiyya (including journalist Ezz el-Din al-Batsh) and near a tent at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah. The Israeli military said it also struck a weapons-manufacturing site in Az-Zawayda and killed Ismail Abu Ful, whom it identified as commander of a Hamas arms-production site, in Maghazi camp. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a joint warning after four paper kites were launched from Gaza over the weekend — the Israeli military said it found nothing suspicious attached to them — declaring that 'if the launches toward Israel do not stop immediately, [the IDF] will act to intensify strikes against those responsible ... and evacuate populations from areas from which kites, drones and balloons are launched.' Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem dismissed the kites as 'children's toys in the refugee camps' and called the threat a 'fabricated pretext'; Palestinian and Israeli analysts quoted by Al Jazeera the next day made the same accusation, with one calling it 'inconceivable that a state possessing a nuclear arsenal considers a paper kite a security threat.' Gaza health officials say more than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, against four Israeli soldiers killed per the IDF.

confidenceReason: Casualty figures corroborated by Gaza civil defense, an Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from the scene, and Arab News wire; the Netanyahu/Katz kite-threat quotes are independently reported by Times of Israel and Al Jazeera.

title: IDF Kills 14-Year-Old Islam Ajjouri During Askar Refugee Camp Raid Near Nablus
detail: On Sunday, August 23, 2026, Israeli forces shot 14-year-old Islam Ahmad Ajjouri in the chest during a military raid on the Askar refugee camp east of Nablus in the northern occupied West Bank. The Palestinian Red Crescent Society said he was evacuated in critical condition and later died of his wounds. Mohammed Abu Kashk, head of the Askar camp services committee, said the teenager was shot as Israeli forces were withdrawing from the camp, adding 'there were no clashes or confrontations that would justify shooting a child and killing him.' The Israeli military said it was reviewing the incident. The killing came two days after West Bank settlers shot dead a 17-year-old near Sa'ir and the IDF killed a retired PA colonel in a Jenin raid, and drew condemnation from Palestinian officials and rights groups; the same weekend the EU's Kaja Kallas separately condemned Israel's E1 settlement tender as a violation of international law.

media.caption: Palestinians mourn 14-year-old Islam Ajjouri, killed by Israeli forces during a raid on Askar refugee camp near Nablus, August 23, 2026

confidenceReason: Death confirmed by the Palestinian Red Crescent Society and corroborated by Arab News, Al Jazeera and Asharq Al-Awsat wire reporting; IDF acknowledged the incident and said it is under review but has not disputed that its forces fired the fatal shot.

title: Palestinian Teen Stabs Israeli Soldier Near Al-Auja in Jordan Valley; IDF Manhunt Ends in Arrest
detail: On Sunday, August 23, 2026, a 16-year-old Palestinian from the village of al-Auja attacked 24-year-old Israeli career soldier Elhanan Hananya as he returned to his car after stopping to buy cigarettes on a highway roughly 8 kilometers north of Jericho in the West Bank's Jordan Valley. Hananya, who was traveling with his pregnant wife, two daughters and father-in-law to celebrate his wedding anniversary, was stabbed several times from behind, suffering a broken shoulder and internal bleeding; he was hospitalized in moderate condition at Shaare Zedek Medical Center and later reported stable and conscious. The IDF launched an hours-long manhunt involving special forces, roadblocks and Israeli Air Force aircraft, and by late afternoon apprehended the suspect, who was handed to the Shin Bet for questioning; troops subsequently operated at the suspect's family home as part of the response.
